summary.text: Son of Apollo and the nymph Cyrene (`cyrene-nymph`) — or, as Hyginus adds, of Abas the Argive king — seer who read his death in the birds yet sailed with Jason and was gored by a boar among the Mariandyni.

story.text: Though augury foretold he would perish on the voyage, Idmon would not stay behind. Among the Mariandyni he went out for straw and a boar gored him; Idas son of Aphareus slew the beast in vengeance.

Apollonius makes him son of Apollo and the nymph Cyrene and sends him from Argos; Hyginus alternatively makes Abas king of Argos his father — the Argive polis carries the residence entry under either parentage.
